data.name: Arafa
data.gender_notes: Arafa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Arafa means 'to travel, to explore'. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'arafa' which means 'to know, to become aware of'. It is also the name of a mountain in Mecca where Muslims gather for pilgrimage. The name evokes a sense of adventure, exploration, and spiritual growth. The name Arafa carries the meaning “Explorer, traveler” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Arafa usually hope their child will grow to embody explorer, traveler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Arafa is also the name of the day in the Hajj pilgrimage when Muslims stand on the plain of Arafat, praying and seeking forgiveness from Allah.
data.etymology: Arafa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Explorer, traveler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arafa total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: عرفة
in_arabic.meaning: عرفة تعني المعرفة أو التعرف على شيء ما
in_arabic.long_meaning: عرفة هو اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، مشتق من الفعل عرف، ومعناه المعرفة أو التعرف على شيء ما. يرتبط هذا الاسم بيوم عرفة، وهو يوم مهم في الإسلام حيث يقف الحجاج على جبل عرفة للتعبير عن معرفتهم وطاعتهم لله. يتميز هذا الاسم بعمقه الديني والثقافي في العالم الإسلامي.

in_urdu.name: عرفہ
in_urdu.meaning: عرفہ کا مطلب ہے علم یا کسی چیز کو پہچاننا
in_urdu.long_meaning: عرفہ ایک علم مؤنث نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ یہ نام عرف فعل سے نکلا ہے، جس کے معنی ہیں علم یا کسی چیز کو پہچاننا۔ یہ نام حج کے دوران عرفات کے دن سے وابستہ ہے، جہاں حجاج جبل عرفات پر کھڑے ہو کر اپنی معرفت اور اطاعت کا اظہار کرتے ہیں۔ یہ نام اسلامی دنیا میں اپنی گہری ثقافتی اور مذہبی اہمیت کے لئے جانا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अरफा
in_hindi.meaning: अरफा का अर्थ है ज्ञान या किसी चीज़ को पहचानना
in_hindi.long_meaning: अरफा एक स्त्रीलिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। यह नाम 'अरफ' क्रिया से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है ज्ञान या किसी चीज़ को पहचानना। यह नाम हज के दौरान अरफात के दिन से जुड़ा हुआ है, जहां हाजी लोग अपनी पहचान और आज्ञाकारिता को व्यक्त करने के लिए अरफात पर्वत पर खड़े होते हैं। यह नाम अपनी गहरी सांस्कृतिक और धार्मिक महत्ता के लिए इस्लामी दुनिया में प्रसिद्ध है।

in_pashto.name: عرفه
in_pashto.meaning: عرفه د پېژندنې یا د یو شی پېژندلو معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: عرفه یو مؤنث نوم دی چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دا نوم د عرف فعل څخه راوځي، چې معنی یې د پېژندنې یا د یو شی پېژندلو څخه دي. دا نوم د حج په دوران کې د عرفات د ورځې سره تړاو لري، چیرته چې حاجیان د خپلې پېژندنې او اطاعت د څرګندولو لپاره د عرفات غره پر مخ ایستي. دا نوم د خپلې ګڼې ثقافتي او مذهبي اهميت له امله په اسلامي نړۍ کې پېژندل شوی دی.

in_english.name: Arafa
in_english.meaning: Arafa means knowledge or recognition of something
in_english.long_meaning: Arafa is a feminine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the verb 'arafa', which means to know or recognize. This name is associated with the Day of Arafah, a significant event in Islam where pilgrims stand on Mount Arafah to express their knowledge and obedience to God. The name carries deep cultural and religious significance in the Islamic world, symbolizing spiritual awareness and devotion. Historically, it reflects the values of knowledge and recognition in Islamic tradition.

data.cultural_impact: During the annual Hajj pilgrimage, millions of Muslims travel from all corners of the world to gather at the sacred Mount Arafat. This event is an opportunity for Muslims to come together as one united Ummah, strengthening bonds and building new relationships. The combining of travel and community is a powerful symbol of unity and solidarity.
data.spiritual_significance: Mount Arafat holds a deep spiritual significance for Muslims. It is believed that Adam and Eve first met there after being expelled from the Garden of Eden. The mountain is also regarded as the place where Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and Prophet Ismail (Ishmael) stood to build the Kaaba. Pilgrims spend the day at Arafat, engaging in prayer and repentance, seeking forgiveness, and asking God for guidance. This day is considered to be the climax of the Hajj pilgrimage and a pivotal moment in a Muslim's spiritual journey.
